title: Modules and controllers
summary: Create an AngularJS module, attach a controller to it and put data on $scope.

quiz.q: What is the status of AngularJS 1.x today?
options: It is the recommended choice for new projects
Support ended in January 2022, so new projects should use modern Angular
It only works on old phones
quiz.explain: AngularJS reached end of life in January 2022. It gets no more fixes, so learn it only to read or maintain existing code.

quiz.q: Complete the call that creates a module named `shopApp` with no dependencies.
quiz.explain: `angular.module(name, [])` creates a module. The empty array is its list of dependencies. Leaving the array out would look up an existing module instead.

quiz.q: Which attribute tells AngularJS which module to start on a page?
quiz.explain: `ng-app="shopApp"` marks the root element and names the module. `ng-controller` attaches a controller to a smaller part of the page.

quiz.q: This controller should show a title, but the page stays empty. Click the faulty line.
quiz.explain: The value must be stored on the scope: `$scope.title = 'My Students';`. A bare `title` is just a stray variable the template cannot see.

exercise.task:
Complete `app.js`.

- Create a module named `studentApp` with an empty dependency array.
- Add a controller named `MainController` to it.
- The controller function receives `$scope`.
- Set `$scope.title` to `'My Students'`.
hints: Start with angular.module('studentApp', []) and chain .controller(...) onto it.
.controller takes the name as a string, then a function. Give the function a $scope parameter and assign to $scope.title inside it.
